Now I can see the exact movement. Original piece (B):
```
row36: 12G 13Y 14Y 15G 16G 17G
row37: 12G 13Y 14Y 15N 16r 17N
row38: 12G 13Y 14Y 15N 16N 17N
row39: 9G 10O 11O 12S 13S 14S
row40: 9G 10O 11O 12S 13S 14S
row41: 9G 10O 11O 12G 13G 14G
```
After clicking the right ring (A):
```
row36: 15G 16Y 17Y 18G 19G 20G
row37: 15G 16Y 17Y 18N 19r 20N
row38: 15G 16Y 17Y 18N 19N 20N
row39: 9G 10O 11O 12O 13O 14O 15S 16S 17S
row40: 9G 10O 11O 12O 13O 14O 15S 16S 17S
row41: 9G 10O 11O 12O 13O 14O 15G 16G 17G
```
So: the top 3 rows (36-38) shifted exactly 3 to the right (12→15). The bottom 3 rows (39-41): the left part (G at column 9, O at 10-11) stayed put, the right part (S/G at 12-14) shifted 3 to the right, and the O body extended to fill 12-14.
So the piece has two "anchors": the G column at column 12 (rows 36-38) moved, but the G column at column 9 (rows 39-41) didn't move.
Hmm, this is a "staircase" piece: the bottom-left block (O+G at columns 9-11, rows 39-41) is the anchor base, and the rest extends to the right. When you click right: the top block (rows 36-38, columns 12-17) moves 3 to the right, and the middle block (S at rows 39-40, columns 12-14) moves 3 to the right, with the O body extending to fill the gap.
Actually, it's simpler: the piece is composed of segments connected by "extensible" O bodies. The O block (rows 39-41, columns 10-11) is between the G anchor (column 9) and the S block (columns 12-14). When you move right, the S block moves 3 to the right, and the O fills the gap.
Similarly, the top block (rows 36-38) sits on top of the S block (columns 12-14) and moves along with it.
So the whole piece is: base G anchor (column 9) + O extensible body + S block + top Y/N block + r tip at (37,16).
The r tip is now at (37,19).
Goal: the red plus is at (31,52). The r tip needs to reach (31,52)? Currently (37,19). Need to go right by 33 and up by 6.
But wait — can the piece move up? The top/bottom clicks on the O container didn't do anything. Maybe vertical movement is controlled by a different container (S, Y, N)? Or maybe the piece can only move horizontally, and the plus is at row 31… the piece's top row is 36. To reach row 31, the piece needs to move up by 5.
Hmm, wait. Maybe the containers control different "parts" of the piece: the O container controls the O body (horizontal extension), and the S/Y/N containers control the other parts? The piece's colors: O (body), S (middle), Y (top), N (top), G (anchor). Four containers: O, S, Y, N.
Maybe: clicking the right ring of the O container extends the O body (moving the S+top block to the right). Clicking the right ring of the S container moves the S block… hmm.
Or, each container is a directional pad for the whole piece, and the O container only responded to right because… no, the left ring click did nothing.
Let me test: click the right ring of the S container (row 57, column 28: S container is at columns 18-30, right ring is at columns 26-28, center (57,28)). And the right ring of the Y container (columns 33-45, right ring center (57,43)). And the right ring of the N container (columns 48-60, right ring center (57,58)).
Let me probe each one and check the diff.
